aAttempts: 1) Read literally: 'write the cell so Sheets parses it as a number ... AND shall protect the cell against manual edits.' A naive implementer treats these as two separate obligations and adds a Sheets ProtectedRange (addProtectedRange via batchUpdate) scoped to the H<row> cell(s), guessing at warningOnly vs hard-block and whether it's asserted once or reasserted every republish - the spec doesn't say.

2) A more indulgent naive reading notices SHEET-TAB-003 already says view-tab content 'is overwritten by design' on republish, and concludes 'protect against manual edits' is already satisfied by that existing regenerate-on-republish behavior - i.e. no new mechanism needed. This reading would NOT flag anything missing, papering over the gap.

3) A third naive reading, anchored to the stated rationale (formulas must evaluate numerically), treats 'protect' as a data-validation rule (setDataValidation restricting the cell to numeric/percent input) so a human literally cannot type non-numeric text into it - a still-unimplemented, different mechanism than either #1 or #2 guessed.
bAttempts: 1) From render_positions + Cell::Value/Cell::Formula + the SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view doc's 'Value typing' paragraph + fmt_ppm: reconstructed spec = 'write Est. Tax Rate as a percent-suffixed value string via a userEnteredValue (not stringValue) so Sheets coerces it to the numeric fraction the post-tax formulas multiply.' No protection clause is inferable - nothing in this code path touches permissions or validation.

2) From runtime::adapters::ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view + runtime::sheets.rs's update_range (valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED): confirms the write path is a plain values-grid write; grepping the whole crates/ tree for protect|Protect|ProtectedRange|setDataValidation turns up zero hits relevant to this cell (only an unrelated duplicate-row guard comment and an unrelated store-lock comment) - a code-only reconstruction would never generate an edit-protection clause.

3) From crates/sheets-view/tests/formula.rs's est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent... test: the only property pinned is 'percent-suffixed, numeric body in [0,1], G*H/G*(1-H) evaluate sensibly' - no test anywhere exercises rejecting or reverting a manual edit, so a test-driven reconstruction also omits any protection clause.
t1SeedAudit.finding: The spec's added 'protect the cell against manual edits' clause is phantom: all three code-only (B-direction) reconstructions converge on the numeric-userEnteredValue-typing behavior alone and never independently produce any manual-edit-protection claim, because no ProtectedRange, data-validation, or edit-rejecting test exists anywhere in the tree. The drift is real and would be caught by any auditor who actually walks the B-direction (grep the write path and tests for a protection primitive) and diffs it against the literal spec sentence. The one honest caveat: an A-direction-only auditor working from the spec text alone has a real chance of NOT catching this, because attempt #2 shows a plausible, generous reading collapses the new clause into the pre-existing, genuinely-implemented SHEET-TAB-003 regenerate-on-republish behavior - a different (eventual, not real-time) guarantee that is easy to mistake for satisfying it. So this self-audit surfaces the seeded gap only when it actually performs the code-side search rather than stopping at a sympathetic spec-only reading.

aAttempts: 1) Read literally: on a transport failure during the marks read-back pass, propagate the error and emit no marks (no partial, no degraded) for that pass; 'runtime' owns carry-forward, retaining the last cached marks. Naive sketch: the read function returns Result and any I/O error is bubbled with '?', never constructing a partial result; the caller (runtime) is responsible for not clobbering its existing marks cache when this Err arrives.

2) Second pass focuses on mechanism: 'propagate' -> Err return (Rust idiom); 'runtime owns carry-forward, retaining the last cached marks' -> the caller must only replace its stored MarksCache on a SUCCESSFUL read, so an early Err return simply leaves the old cache variable untouched (replace-on-success pattern) - an assumption about implementation shape, not stated verbatim in the spec.

3) Third pass stresses 'no partial or degraded marks': even if some symbols resolved before a mid-pass transport failure, the WHOLE pass must yield nothing - naive design accumulates per-poll results only in a local structure and discards it via the same early '?' return, so no half-populated result ever escapes the function.
bAttempts: 1) From sheets_view::read_marks (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs ~825-845): the poll loop calls client.read_price_pass()? each iteration; any Err propagates immediately, before any MarksProduced is built, and the local 'latest' accumulator is dropped. Reconstructed: 'on a transport error at any poll, propagate Err and never return a MarksProduced (no partial/degraded) for that call' - matches spec exactly.

2) From runtime::cycle::run_cycle (crates/runtime/src/cycle.rs ~305-335): calls read_marks(...)? - on Err, run_cycle itself returns Err before constructing a new MarksCache; the doc comment right above it states the caller retains its prior cached marks and re-injects them next cycle. Reconstructed: 'the per-cycle marks cache is replaced only on a successful read-back; a transport failure leaves the existing cache untouched for the caller to reuse' - matches spec's 'runtime owns carry-forward' clause exactly.

3) From the tests (sheets-view/tests/marks.rs::transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks, asserting result.is_err() under set_read_fails(true); runtime/tests/cold_start.rs::the_price_pass_on_a_fresh_workbook_is_empty_not_an_error, pinning that a legitimately-empty pass is Ok, NOT an error): reconstructed 'a transport failure surfaces as Err, distinct from a legitimately-empty non-erroring read' - matches spec's implicit boundary.
t1ControlAudit.finding: SHEET-MARK-006's text, the read_marks/run_cycle implementation, and both crates' tests agree precisely on all three clauses (propagate-Err, no-partial-marks, cache-replaced-only-on-success so runtime retains the last good cache). No drift surfaced in either direction; this spec was not touched by the seeding for this task.
